page: Hetzner Cloud cax11 is an entry-level, ARM-based virtual server instance powered by the Ampere Altra processor family. It features 2 shared vCPUs utilizing the Neoverse-N1 architecture running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of RAM. Local storage is provided via a 40 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance operates under a QEMU hypervisor. The CPU configuration does not support hyper-threading, providing one thread per physical core, and includes hardware-assisted AES cryptography while lacking AVX and AMX instruction sets.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the cax11 is positioned at the lower end of the spectrum, reflecting its shared-resource model. Single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests is average, but multi-core scaling is weak, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1734.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 1535.95. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached write speeds of 14.07 GB/sec and read speeds of 23.72 GB/sec. These metrics suggest a clear tradeoff between dedicated compute power and resource density.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the cax11 offers an economical entry point into ARM64 cloud computing, making it suitable for lightweight workloads that do not require sustained high-performance CPU or memory throughput. Appropriate use cases include basic web serving, development environments, lightweight background tasks, and small-scale database operations.
